explain:
Regression predicts a numeric target; classification predicts a category or probability; clustering groups examples without supplied class targets. Define the decision and cost of errors before choosing the method. An always-majority classifier can have high accuracy on an imbalanced dataset while missing every rare event. Establish a simple baseline, then evaluate whether a more complex model improves the outcome you actually need.

Linear models make an explicit weighted combination of features. Trees split the feature space into decision regions; ensembles combine trees to reduce particular errors, but add size and operational cost. Clustering methods depend on distance, scale and assumptions about cluster shape. A cluster label is not automatically a ground-truth business category. Feature engineering and preprocessing are part of fitting and must respect the same split boundaries as model parameters.

Use training data to fit, validation data to select settings, and a held-out test set for the final declared evaluation. If you repeatedly pick changes because they improve test accuracy, that set has become a validation set. Time-dependent tasks need chronological splits, and related entities may need group splits. Fit scalers, vocabularies and feature selectors only on training observations, then apply the fitted transformation to held-out rows.

The training capstone uses explicit non-overlapping synthetic splits and a fixed architecture, seed, step count and learning rate. Its perfect tiny-fixture accuracy establishes only that the implementation solves this separated toy problem. It says nothing about generalization to real customer data. The retrieval capstone separately measures relevance recovery and abstention, showing why model loss, retrieval quality and generated-answer faithfulness must not be collapsed into one score.
example: A preprocessing scaler is fitted before the dataset is split. Identify statistics computed from held-out examples. Fit the scaler only on training data inside the evaluation pipeline. Repeat selection using a validation split, reserving an untouched final test. Result: The corrected score measures a cleaner generalization question rather than information leakage.
takeaway: Unexpectedly perfect results call for a split and feature-provenance audit. A train/test gap can result from leakage, distribution shift, insufficient data, overfitting or an unsuitable task definition.

Q: Choose linear, tree and unsupervised baselines by their objective
explain:
A model family defines a representation and a fitted objective, not an automatic product decision. Linear regression predicts a numerical target and can minimize squared residuals. Logistic classification maps a score to a probability using a sigmoid in the binary case and is often trained by log loss. Converting a probability to an action requires an independently chosen threshold and cost policy. Inspect scaling, feature availability and regularization before discarding a simple baseline.

A decision tree repeatedly partitions features using learned rules, producing predictions within the resulting leaves. Deep trees can fit tiny partitions and memorize training artifacts. Limiting depth, leaf size or other complexity controls changes that behavior. A random forest aggregates varied trees to reduce some variance; boosting fits additional learners sequentially against an objective. Neither an ensemble nor a familiar algorithm name repairs data leakage. Select complexity and hyperparameters using validation, not the final test labels.

K-means addresses a different question: assign points to a chosen number of centroids under a within-cluster distance objective. Alternate between nearest-centroid assignment and recomputing centroids from assigned points. Scale changes the geometry, initialization can change the final solution, and clusters need not correspond to business categories. For points 0, 1, 9 and 10 with starting centers 0 and 10, nearest-center groups become {0,1} and {9,10}, yielding new centers 0.5 and 9.5. That calculation is not evidence of which customers should receive permission or service.

PCA instead finds variance directions in appropriately centered training data, often through a matrix decomposition. A high-variance direction can reflect noise or an irrelevant magnitude, while a low-variance feature can still matter for prediction. Fit every learned transformation on the permitted training partition, compare a task-relevant baseline and retain validation/error slices. Use the complete digits experiment for actual held-out fitting; the four-point calculation only explains one clustering update.
example: Execute one K-means assignment/update on four points. Then multiply one feature by a large unit conversion and inspect how a two-dimensional nearest-center choice can change. Keep that geometric effect separate from supervised target correctness.
takeaway: Choose a method for a defined prediction or representation objective, and evaluate the resulting decision under an appropriate split and cost model.

Q: Model selection, leakage, uncertainty and a measured CPU baseline
explain:
The bundled digits dataset supplies 1,797 handwritten 8 by 8 images, making this a real dataset experiment beyond a generated linearly separable classifier. Fix the row indices for train, validation and test before fitting anything. The reference uses 1,078 training, 359 validation and 360 test rows. Fit StandardScaler only inside the training pipeline and reuse its learned transformation. Validation chooses among three regularization values using multiclass log loss. The test labels cannot select the best value or fix preprocessing. A pipeline prevents some accidental preprocessing mistakes; it cannot make an inappropriate split representative.

State the generalization question before reporting accuracy. A random stratified row split measures this particular row-sampling design. It does not establish independence from handwriting authors, because the loader does not provide the writer identities needed to enforce that split. For customer or document datasets, put all examples from one correlated group on one side of a split. For forecasting, preserve time and prevent features from seeing the future. Repeatedly inspecting a test set and altering the system turns that set into another validation set.

Compare the selected model with a most-frequent-class baseline on exactly the same test rows. Save the confusion matrix and the indices of errors rather than retaining only one average. A Wilson interval estimates uncertainty in a binomial accuracy under independent-sample assumptions; 98 correct answers out of 100 do not imply a population accuracy exactly equal to 98 percent. A paired bootstrap resamples corresponding row-wise differences between systems, preserving their evaluation pairing. Correlated samples and many repeated comparisons need a different design; a random seed is not a correction for those biases.

Keep probability quality, corruption robustness and performance separate. Log loss penalizes confident mistakes but is not a pure measure of calibration. If adding a calibrator, fit it without using the final test labels and inspect reliability bins with their sample counts. The supplied middle-row corruption is a declared stress slice, not a future production population. Warm up the model, constrain numerical library threads and measure repeated single-row calls with an explicit timer. The result includes Python/sklearn overhead and describes local CPU latency only. It cannot justify a GPU throughput, concurrent-service or foundation-model finetuning claim.
example: A model is correct on 98 of 100 approximately independent examples. Compute the observed proportion 0.98. Use the Wilson denominator 1 + 1.96²/100. Compute the center and half-width from the binomial formula. Report an approximate 95% interval of 0.9300 to 0.9945 with the assumptions. Result: The observed 98% is an estimate; the interval does not prove performance on another distribution.
takeaway: When performance looks unexpectedly perfect, inspect duplicate/group leakage, feature construction timing and preprocessing fit indices before increasing the model size.
